doc.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007

title: Nola's Studio jam sessions and meeting Bob Wilber
summary: He joined New York jam sessions at Nola's Studio where he first met Bob Wilber and imitated Johnny Dodds.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Lester was sort of past then, but it was my favorite, you know I like the old stuff. And so I didn’t do much with the dance band. I think I played a little flute, lousy flute, and a little solo on something. But so what I did was by that time I’m in New York and I’m starting to play, and I got in with a crowd, you know a crowd of guys like my age and maybe a couple of guys from the Jazz Club in Brooklyn. And what happened was there used to be a Lindy’s or whatever it was called, it was on Broadway, high 40s, above Times Square, and above that was Nola’s.

They’re on 57th if they’re still around. But I rehearsed there with Louis Armstrong. So anyhow the Nola’s Studio, you could rent. You could rent a room, it had a piano, and the deal was everybody would kick in some money, two, three dollars, whatever it was, and rent a room for an hour or two hours, and have a jam session. And we did that. And there
was, you know, really feeling our way and a part of that scene was Bob Wilber. That’s where I first met Bob Wilber. Bob Wilber, by the way, looks much better today than he did then. He was a skinny —

Skinny, pale, with sort of bad hair, wavy, curly hair you know. And he looked like a nerd. But he played wonderfully. I said Jesus Christ he scared me to death. And I was sort of like, in retrospect I was sort of a nature boy, you know, with the red notes and a lot of wails and wooo. Soulful. You’re trying to imitate Johnny Dodds. I mean I didn’t — I liked Benny Goodman but I didn’t aspire to that kind of clarinet that I wanted to play. But Johnny Dodds was my hero for a long time.
